caption_verbatim: Fig. 2 | caption_from_image: ANATOMY Embryology Basic embryology of the spine A.After the folding of the embryo during the third week, the paraxial mesoderm migrates to envelope the notochord and divides into "sclerotomes." B. Each sclerotome differentiates into a cranial, loosely arranged portion and a caudal compact portion. C. The compact caudal portion of each sclerotome fuses with the loose cranial portion of the adjacent sclerotome to form the vertebral bodies. The most cranial part of each compact portion forms an intervertebral disk. D. The neural arches are formed by a dorsal migration of sclerotome elements completing the membranous vertebral column. This is followed by chondrification and eventually ossification of the vertebrae. SCLEROTOMES DIVISIONS FORMATIONS Occipital 1st 2nd 3rd 4th "Proatlas" basiocciput Exoccipital centers (jugular tubercles) Hypocentrum: Anterior tubercle clivus Centrum: Apical ligament, apex of dens Neural Arch: Ventral rostral : Occipital condyles, third cond, alar and cruciate ligaments, U-shape of foramen magnum Dorsal caudal : Posterior arch of atlas C1, lateral atlantal masses Spinal 1st Hypocentrum: Atlas anterior arch Centrum: Dens Neural Arch: Posterior inferior atlas arch Spinal 2nd Hypocentrum: Disapears Centrum: Body of axis Neural Arch: Facets, posterior arch of axis

caption_verbatim: Fig. 2 | caption_from_image: ANATOMY Technics RX Lateral view: 85-90% of cervical injuries are evident in lateral view. -Check aligment: 3 imaginary contour lines: anterior, posterior and spinolaminar. - Atlantodental interval: <3mm adult, <5 mm child. Suspect transverse ligament disruption if these limits are exceeded. - Check prevertebral space. At level C2 < 7mm. If widened suspect hematoma secondary to a fracture. - Check for fanning of the spinous processes. - Check for an abrupt change in angulation. Oblique view: is considered laminar view. Odontoid / Open mouth view: to evaluate an area that is difficult to visualize in the lateral view. Alignment of the lateral masses of C1 with respect to the odontoid process. Anteroposterior view: The least useful view from clinical standpoint. A straight line should connect the spinous processes bisecting the cervical spine. If this is not seen consider a rotation injury. Flexion and extension: views for assesment to soft tissue injury. TC Multidetector CT scans with volumetric reconstructions. If plain radiograph findings are negative but clinical suspicion for fracture is high, films should be followed by CT. MRI MRI is more sensitive for soft tissue injury than radiography. Ultrasound US should be considered the initial imaging modality of choice for investigating the spinal cord and CVJ in newborns.

Line extrapolated along dorsal surface of the clivus Line should fall tangent to, or intersect, the posterior one third of the odontoid Chamberlain's line Posterior margin of hard palate to opisthion Tip of the odontoid should be no more than 5 mm above this line; anterior arch of C1 lies below. caption_verbatim: Fig. 7 | caption_from_image: ANATOMY Craniometry LANDMARKS, LINES AND ANGLES Basal Welcher angle Clivus-canal angle Atlanto-occipital joint axis angle Landmarks Basal Welcher angle: Angle subtendend by the junction of the nasion-tuberculum and tuberculum-basion tangents. Average= 134º-135º Minimum= 121º Maximum = 148º-149º Platybasia if > 150º. When this angle is less than 123 º is called kyphotic skull. If the angle is greater than 143 º is called platybasia. Clivus-canal angle: Angle formed at junction of Wackenheim's line and posterior vertebral body line. Range= 150º in flexion to 180º in extension < 150º considered abdnormal. When less than 150 º can be ventral compression of the CVJ, between the medulla oblongata and spinal cord, which is optimal evaluation with MRI. Atlanto-occipital joint axis angle: Angle formed at the junction of lines traversing the atlanto-occipital joints. Average=124º-127º. May approach 180º in severe occipital condyle hypoplasia These tangents typically intersect at the center of the odontoid process when the condyles are symmetric.

caption_verbatim: Fig. 9 | caption_from_image: CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS Atlanto-occipital Atlanto-occipital assimilation - Complete/partial failure of segmentation between skull + 1st cervical vertebra. - Most common anomaly involving the CVJ encountered in 0,14%-0,25% of the population. - Violation of Chamberlain line. - Clivus-canal angle decreased. - May be associated with : fusion of C2-C3. - Association: congenital abnormalities 20%, congenital external ear anomalies ,cervical ribs,urinary tract. Complications: atlantoaxial subluxation 50%, sudden death. C 1 CT and MRI with atlanto-occipital assimilation. Coronal and sagittal views demonstrate fusion of the lateral C1-masses (1) to the occipital condyles (C). Platybasia - Increased Welcher basal angle>143º-145º. - May be associated with basilar invagination. Basilar invagination - Abnormally high position of vertebral column prolapsing into skull base. - To evaluate: Chamberlain, McGregor,Fishgold lines. Sagittal MRI shows patient with platybasia and basilar invagination associated.

caption_verbatim: Fig. 13 | caption_from_image: CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS Atlas and axis Atlas Axis CT with posterior atlas arch hypoplasia (arrow). T2-sagittal and T1-coronal weighted MR shows os odontoideum anomaly. The anterior arch of the atlas maintains a normal relationship with the os (arrow). Note the well-cortciated upper margin of the axis. Abnormalities of the posterior arch It is rare - Posterior atlas arch rachischisis (4%). LOCATION: midline (97%), lateral through sulcus of vertebral artery (3%). - Absence of arch-canal line. - Superimposed on odontoid process/axis body simulating a fracture (open mouth odontoid view) Abnormalities of the anterior arch 1- Isolated anterior arch rachischisis (0'1%). 2- Split atlas= anterior+posterior arch rachischisis - Plump rounded anterior arch overlapping the odontoid process making identification of predental space impossible. - Duplicated anterior margins. Persisten osciculum terminale = Bergman ossicle. -Unfused odontoid process >12 years of age. DXD: type 1 odontoid fracture. Odontoid aplasia ( extremely rare) Os odontoideum = independent os cephalad to axis body in location of odontoid process. - absence of odontoid process. - anterior arch of atlas hypertrophic + situated too far posterior in relation to axis body. - Complications: atlantoaxial instability. - DDx: Type 2 odontoid fracture (uncorticated margin).

caption_verbatim: Fig. 15 | caption_from_image: CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS Syndromes Klippel-Feil Syndrome -Short neck -Low hairline -Limited neck mobility -Segmentation abnormalities most often involving:C2-C3 and C5-C6. -In addtion: basilar invagination, odontoid hypoplasia, atlanto-occipital assimilation, platybasia, Chiari I malformation. - >50% scoliosis >20º - ≈ 14% ventriculoseptal defects. -66% genitourinary tract abnormalities. -Association between segmentation and dysraphic anomalies. 4-year-old child, Klippel-Feil Syndrome affected with basilar invagination. Achondroplasia - Most common short limbed dwarfism. - A point mutation on the gen that encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor-3. - Abnormalities: regions through encondral ossification. - Calvarium NORMAL/ skull base, facial bones,foramen magnum UNDERDEVELOPED. - TEAR DROP configuration: Constricted foramen magnum, odontoid dysplasia, basiocciput hypoplasia, decrease in basal angle. Sagittal T2-WI MR, 2-year-old child with constricted foramen magnum. Osteogenesis imperfecta - Hereditary disorder: defect in collagen production resulting in osteoporosis. - Repetitive microfractures—infolding the occipital condyles with elevation of the clivus and the posterior cranial fossa. - Basilar impression—"Darth vader" appearance. Down syndrome -Atlanto-occipital 61%+ atlanto-axial instability 9-30%/ secondary to a combination of ligamentous laxity and associated osseous anomalies. - Atlanto-dental interval >5mm. Mucopolysaccharidoses - Inherited lysosomal storage disorders caused by enzymes required for degradation of glycosaminoglycans. - TYPE IV: MORQUIO—abnormalities at the CVJ major cause of morbidity and mortality. - Ligamentous instability. - Hypoplastic/dysplastic odontoid process. - Soft tissue thickening arround the dens (hypo/iso T1/hypo T2) non-ossified fibrocartilage. - Compression of the cord by the posterior atlas arch. Sagittal T2-WI MR, 3-year-old with constricted foramen magnum.
